payload.title: The SET rule treats any if or case that compares authMode with any literal as a guard, so a credential write inside the mtls-cert branch, in an else branch, under `!== 'none'`, or in any case clause is reported as guarded
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/security-boundary-adapter.ts:784-802 (sitsInAuthModeBranch: any ancestor `if` whose test compares authMode with a literal counts, whichever branch holds the write; any string-literal `case` of switch (authMode) counts)
tools/aria-adapters/security-boundary-adapter.ts:805-824 (comparesAuthModeWithLiteral accepts == === != !== against any string literal; it never asks which mode the literal is)
libs/backend-common/src/nats/nats-connection.factory.ts:147 (NatsAuthMode is 'mtls-cert' | 'token' | 'user-pass' | 'none'; only token and user-pass may put a credential on the CONNECT frame)

libs/backend-common/src/nats/nats-connection.factory.ts:279-291 (the factory states that mtls-cert must leave user/pass/token unset; the guard that enforces it is the then-branch for token and user-pass)
tools/aria-adapters/security-boundary-adapter.nats.test.ts:79-107 (no pinned variant writes a credential inside the mtls-cert branch, an else branch or a negated comparison)
payload.rule_violated: ADR-015 (cert-is-identity): no user, pass or token reaches the CONNECT frame under mTLS; the rule's own manifest defect_claim says the write must sit outside a branch on the chosen mode.
payload.notes: Changing the factory to `if (authMode === 'mtls-cert') { options.user = authUser; }`, or to `if (authMode === 'token') { options.token = authToken; } else { options.user = authUser; }`, or to `if (authMode !== 'none') { options.pass = authPass; }` writes credentials in the mode ADR-015 forbids, and the rule reports nothing because each write has an enclosing authMode comparison. Reproduced by running the adapter's own sitsInAuthModeBranch and comparesAuthModeWithLiteral on those factories: all three gave no finding, and so did a write in `case 'mtls-cert':` of a switch on authMode. The guard that is itself the violation is therefore a shape the rule is blind to. Close condition: Reduce a write's guard to the mode it runs under: it counts only in the then-branch (or the matching case) of an equality with a credential-bearing mode (token, user-pass), with the mode names owned by tools/gates/nats-connection-owner.ts, and the nats test adds a finding variant for a write in the mtls-cert branch, in `case 'mtls-cert':`, in an else branch and under `!== 'none'`, with the real factory staying clean. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 1). Verified at head a47dc4d57c of open pull request #2134; the cited code is not on main until that pull request merges.
